# Jubilees Chapter 35 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Rebekah's deathbed testament to Esau and Jacob

---

**35:1** In the first year of the seventh week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Rebekah called her son Jacob and commanded him with regard to Esau his brother, saying to him:

**35:2** "I have been observing and seeing, my son, all the deeds of Esau thy brother, and I know that his deeds are evil and full of wickedness. He pays no attention to the word of his father and the word of his mother.

**35:3** And thou, my son, take care of thy soul and show thyself upright in everything, and thou shalt find grace before God and before men.

**35:4** And take care of Esau, that he do not rise against thee, and that there be no quarrel between you, for it would be an abomination before God if the blood of brothers were shed.

**35:5** And I want thee to know, my son, that all the children of Belial rise up against Israel and all the nations.

**35:6** And I am afraid concerning all the deeds of Esau thy brother, lest he do harm to thee and thou be destroyed. So observe him and fear him; but do not seek his destruction.

**35:7** And know that from the time I saw thee in thy mother's womb I have loved thee with all my heart and soul. And I have loved thee as I have loved no other of my children; for thou art truly the beloved son."

**35:8** And Rebekah wept bitterly. And Jacob wept too.

**35:9** And Rebekah said: "O LORD God, let me not see the day when Jacob my son dies before me, for my heart and my soul would be grieved exceedingly."

**35:10** And she sent and called Esau and said to him: "I have something to say to thee, my son." And he came to her.

**35:11** And she said to him: "I have a request to make of thee, my son; wilt thou hear my voice?"

**35:12** And Esau said to her: "I will hear, my mother." And she said to him: "I am asking thee, my son, and entreat thee, to honor thy brother Jacob and to love him."

**35:13** "For I love thee both together, but this especially: that thou do not harm or hurt him all the days of thy life and as long as thou livest. For his enemy I am not able to endure."

**35:14** And Esau said: "I will do as thou sayest, and I will not harm my brother Jacob. I have been reconciled to him. And I love him more than my own soul."

**35:15** And she said: "Bless the LORD thy God who has given thee this spirit of reconciliation, for thou hast sworn before the LORD that thou wilt not harm thy brother Jacob. Swear to me by God that thou wilt keep this word."

**35:16** And Esau swore to Rebekah by God that he would not harm Jacob for all his life.

**35:17** And Rebekah called Jacob and told him the news that Esau had been reconciled to him and had sworn to him before God. And she rejoiced greatly.

**35:18** And Rebekah fell sick and died, and Jacob and Esau mourned her greatly.

**35:19** And she was buried in the double cave at Mamre with Isaac her husband. And all her sons and the sons of Jacob buried her with great weeping and mourning.

**35:20** And in the second year of the first week of the forty-sixth jubilee, Isaac died. And his sons Jacob and Esau buried him.

**35:21** And Esau departed to Edom, and Jacob dwelt at Hebron. And Jacob sent his sons' food to Esau whenever they lacked.

**35:22** And Esau sent gifts and greetings to Jacob whenever he passed by. And there was peace between them all the days of Isaac and Rebecca.

---

*EMET notes: Rebekah's testament (vv.1-19) is a Jubilees-unique section with no Genesis parallel. It is one of the few places in Jubilees where a female character is given extended speech. The reconciliation between Jacob and Esau is engineered by Rebekah here, unlike in Genesis. Her death and burial at Machpelah is also unique to Jubilees.*
